answer: A credible sybil defense is to require each agent to lock scarce, transferable collateral before it can trade, then slash that bond when a dispute proves fraud. Creating a hundred identities no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must fund a hundred bonds, keep capital immobilized, and risk losing it. Honest agents can use repeated, costly participation to build reputation, while a newcomer’s claim remains untrusted until it survives scrutiny. A voyage through the market earns trust; an echo of copied identities does not turn an oasis into proof.
